reports.title: Baseline history – Initial diagnosis Multiple Myeloma

sections.name: Medical history
sections.content: The 60-year-old patient presents for evaluation of back pain existing for approximately 4 months and progressive fatigue. No relevant prior illnesses. Non-smoker. No regular alcohol consumption. Employed as an engineer.

sections.name: Family history
sections.content: Mother deceased from gastric carcinoma. Father had myocardial infarction at age 72. No known hematologic malignancies in the family.

reports.title: Bone marrow biopsy – Initial diagnosis

sections.name: Question
sections.content: Suspected multiple myeloma. Bone marrow trephine biopsy from 14.03.2019. Macroscopy: Two trephine cores, each approximately 1.5 cm in length. Processing: HE, Giemsa, Gomori, PAS, immunohistochemical stains.

sections.name: Findings
sections.content: Hypercellular bone marrow trephine core (cellularity approx. 70–80%) with diffuse and nodularly confluent infiltration by mature plasma cells. Infiltration grade: approx. 60% of nucleated cells. Immunohistochemistry: CD138+, MUM1+, kappa light chains dominant, lambda negative. No evidence of amyloid-like material. Reticulin fibers grade 1 (MF-1) according to WHO.

sections.name: FISH result
sections.content: FISH analysis (plasma cell gating): - del(17p): POSITIVE (TP53 deletion in 42% of cells) – high‑risk cytogenetics - t(4;14): negative - t(14;16): negative - 1q21 gain: negative Conclusion: Detection of del(17p) as a high‑risk marker.

sections.name: Diagnosis
sections.content: Multiple myeloma, IgG kappa light chain. ISS stage II (β2‑microglobulin 4.1 mg/l, albumin 3.6 g/dl). R‑ISS stage III (ISS II + del(17p) + elevated LDH).

reports.title: Whole‑body CT – Staging

sections.name: Findings
sections.content: Whole‑body low‑dose CT from 18.03.2019. Skull: No definitive osteolytic lesions. Spine: Multiple small lytic lesions at BWK7, BWK9 and LWK2, max. diameter 8 mm. No pathological fracture. Pelvis: Two small osteolyses in the left Os ilium (each approx. 5 mm). Long bones: No suspicious findings. Conclusion: Osseous manifestations of multiple myeloma in the spine and pelvis. No evidence of pathological fracture.

reports.title: Whole‑body MRI – Staging

sections.name: Findings
sections.content: Whole‑body MRI (1.5 Tesla, STIR and T1w sequences) from 20.03.2019. Bone marrow: Diffuse involvement pattern in the axial skeleton with decreased T1 signal and increased STIR signal. Focal lesions at BWK7 and LWK2 confirmed, each without spinal cord compression. Extramedullary manifestation: Not detected. Conclusion: Diffuse medullary involvement consistent with multiple myeloma. No extramedullary disease.

reports.title: Physician's letter – Initial diagnosis and treatment planning

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Hematologic diagnoses:
Multiple myeloma, IgG light chain kappa (initial diagnosis 03/2019)  
ISS stage II, R-ISS stage III  
High‑risk cytogenetics: del(17p) positive  
Osseous manifestations: osteolyses T7, T9, L2, left ilium  

Comorbidities:  
Arterial hypertension, well controlled with medication  
No relevant cardiac pre‑existing conditions

sections.name: History
sections.content: The 60‑year‑old patient presents after external diagnostics for planning of first‑line therapy. Since November 2018 progressive back pain, B‑symptoms denied. Incidental finding of anemia (Hb 9.8 g/dl) by the primary care physician.

sections.name: Clinical examination
sections.content:
ECOG performance status: 1.
General condition/nutrition: Slightly reduced general condition, good nutritional status.  
Organ: No jaundice, no palpable lymphadenopathy. No hepatosplenomegaly.

sections.name: Previous therapy
sections.content: No prior therapy for the myeloma.

sections.name: Therapy plan
sections.content:
Start first‑line therapy with VRd (Bortezomib/Lenalidomide/Dexamethasone) from 25.03.2019, planned 6 cycles of 21 days each.
Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m² subcutaneously on days 1, 4, 8, 11.  
Lenalidomide 25 mg/day orally on days 1–14.  
Dexamethasone 40 mg orally on days 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 12.  
Bisphosphonate: Zometa (Zoledronic acid) 4 mg intravenously every 4 weeks.

sections.name: Procedure
sections.content:
Follow‑up in 3 weeks for remission assessment after cycle 1 VRd.
Next laboratory check: 28.03.2019.

reports.title: Tumor board decision – Initial diagnosis MM, treatment planning

sections.name: Reason for discussion
sections.content: Initial diagnosis of a multiple myeloma, IgG light chain kappa, in a 60‑year‑old patient. ISS II, R‑ISS III, high‑risk cytogenetics del(17p). ECOG 1. Eligible for transplantation.

sections.name: Previous therapy
sections.content: No prior therapy.

sections.name: Decision
sections.content:
Consensus: First‑line therapy with VRd (Bortezomib/Lenalidomide/Dexamethasone) × 6 cycles, followed by autologous stem cell transplantation after high‑dose melphalan (200 mg/m²).
High‑risk cytogenetics del(17p) taken into account – no study available that addresses this situation at present.  
Bisphosphonate therapy with zoledronic acid. Remission assessment after 3 cycles. Goal: ≥VGPR before ASCT.

reports.title: Physician's letter – Inpatient treatment: Neutropenic sepsis

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content: Multiple myeloma, IgG LK kappa (ED 03/2019) Neutropenic sepsis under VRd cycle 3 (inpatient 15–20.06.2019)

sections.name: Course
sections.content: Inpatient admission on 15.06.2019 for fever 39.8 °C and known neutropenia. Leukocytes 0.8 G/l, neutrophils 0.2 G/l. CRP 18.4 mg/dl. Empiric antibiotic therapy with Piperacillin/Tazobactam 4.5 g i.v. Blood cultures: no pathogen detected. Rapid defervescence within 48 h. Leukocyte reconstitution by discharge on 20.06.2019 (Lk 3.1 G/l). Lenalidomide in cycle 3 discontinued from day 11. Dose reduction to 15 mg/d established for all subsequent cycles.

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: Discharge 20.06.2019. Extended treatment pause for reconstitution. Cycle 4 VRd earliest early September 2019. Outpatient follow‑up 15.07.2019.

sections.name: Current course
sections.content: Patient in good general condition. Complete recovery after sepsis episode. Blood count normalized: Lk 4.4 G/l, neutrophils 2.8 G/l. No fever, no infection. sections.content: Multiple myeloma, IgG LK kappa (ED 03/2019) ISS II, R‑ISS III, del(17p) Therapy: VRd cycles 1–3, VGPR

sections.name: Therapy course
sections.content:
Under VRd after 3 cycles good response: IgG decreased from initial 42 g/l to 8.3 g/l. Immunofixation still positive. Free kappa light chains within normal range.

Tolerability: Peripheral neuropathy grade 1 (tingling in fingertip tips, no functional limitation). Fatigue grade 2. No gastrointestinal toxicity. Neutropenia grade 2 in cycle 2, treated supportively.  

On 15.06.2019: Neutropenic sepsis with fever >38.5 °C, inpatient admission for 5 days. Antibiotic therapy with Piperacillin/Tazobactam. Complete recovery. Due to sepsis episode dose reduction of lenalidomide to 15 mg from cycle 4.

reports.title: Physician letter – response after 6 cycles VRd, ASCT planning

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple Myeloma, IgG κ light chain (ED 03/2019)
After 6 cycles VRd: VGPR  
Planning autologous stem cell transplantation

sections.name: Response after VRd
sections.content:
After 6 cycles VRd:
- IgG: 5,1 g/l (baseline 42 g/l)  
- Immunofixation in serum: positive (weak)  
- Free light chains kappa: 18 mg/l (within normal range)  
- Kappa/Lambda ratio: 2,1 (slightly elevated)  
Assessment: VGPR (very good partial response)  

Cumulative Bortezomib dose: 6 cycles × 4 Gaben × 1,3 mg/m² × 1,73 m² KOF = ca. 55,0 mg total.  
Cumulative Lenalidomid dose: 3 cycles × 14 days × 25 mg + 3 cycles × 14 days × 15 mg = 1.680 mg total.

sections.name: Stem cell mobilization
sections.content: Stem cell mobilization performed with G‑CSF (Filgrastim) and Plerixafor. Collected CD34+ count: 8,2 × 10^6 cells/kg KG (sufficient for 2 transplantations).

sections.name: Therapy plan
sections.content: High‑dose melphalan (200 mg/m²) with subsequent autologous stem cell transplantation planned for 02/2020. Conditioning: melphalan 100 mg/m² day -2 and day -1 (total dose 200 mg/m²; with KOF 1,73 m² = 346 mg total). Transfusions: 2 EK intraoperatively due to Hb drop to 7,1 g/dl.

reports.title: Skeletal MRI – Follow‑up control 6 months post‑ASCT

sections.name: Full report
sections.content:
Clinical information: MM IgG kappa, after HD‑Melphalan + ASCT 02/2020, CR since 04/2020. Lenalidomide maintenance ongoing.

Question: Follow‑up of bone‑marrow involvement. Comparison with previous examination (MRI 20.03.2019).

Previous imaging: Whole‑body MRI 20.03.2019.

Findings: Whole‑body MRI (1.5 Tesla, STIR and T1‑weighted) from 12.08.2020.  
Bone marrow: Marked regression of the previously diffuse involvement pattern. T1 signal approximately normal in the axial skeleton. No definite STIR hyper‑intensity pattern detectable any more.  
Focal lesions: T7 vertebral body lesion regressing (now 4 mm, previously 8 mm), L2 vertebral body lesion no longer clearly delineated.  
Extramedullary manifestation: Not detectable.  
Conclusion: Marked remission of myelomatous bone‑marrow involvement. No evidence of progression or new lesions.

reports.title: PET‑CT – relapse staging

sections.name: Full report
sections.content:
Clinical information: MM IgG kappa, suspected relapse. New osteolysis LWK4 on skeletal CT 05.05.2022.

Question: Metabolic activity of the osseous lesions. Exclusion of extramedullary manifestation.

Prior imaging: No prior study of this modality available.

Findings: PET‑CT from 06.05.2022.
LWK4: FDG‑avid lesion (SUVmax 4,8), metabolically active, corresponding to the described CT osteolysis.
Other osseous manifestations: BWK7 without relevant FDG uptake (SUVmax 1,4 – residual scar process).
Extramedullary manifestation: Not detectable.
Conclusion: Singular metabolically active osseous lesion LWK4, compatible with focal myeloma relapse. No extra‑osseous myeloma.

sections.name: Full report
sections.content:
Clinical information: MM IgG kappa, under Dara‑Rd. Rising IgG and FLK values. Increasing L4 lumbar pain.

Prior imaging: Skeletal CT 05.05.2022.

reports.title: Tumor board decision – Triple‑class‑exposed relapse, CAR‑T planning

sections.name: Reason for discussion
sections.content: Third relapse of a multiple myeloma, IgG kappa light chain (diagnosed 03/2019). Patient triple‑class‑exposed (PI, IMiD, CD38 mAb). Planning next line of therapy.

sections.name: Prior therapy
sections.content:
03/2019–01/2020: VRd × 6 cycles → VGPR
02/2020: high‑dose melphalan (200 mg/m²) + autologous SCT → CR  
04/2020–04/2022: lenalidomide maintenance (10 mg/d)  
05/2022–07/2023: daratumumab + lenalidomide + dexamethasone (Dara‑Rd) → VGPR → progression  
09/2023–ongoing: isatuximab + pomalidomide + dexamethasone (Isa‑Pd) → PR → now renewed increase

sections.name: Decision
sections.content:
Consensus: The patient meets the criteria for a BCMA‑directed CAR‑T cell therapy.
Approved BCMA‑CAR‑T products in Germany (as of 02/2024): idecabtagene vicleucel (Ide‑cel / Abecma) and ciltacabtagene autoleucel (Cilta‑cel / Carvykti).  
Diagnostics before CAR‑T: current CT/PET‑CT, bone‑marrow biopsy with immunophenotyping, BCMA expression (FACS), echocardiography, pulmonary function, infection serology (CMV, EBV, HSV, HBV, HCV, HIV), complete blood count and coagulation.  
Leukapheresis recommended promptly (bridging with pomalidomide/dexamethasone until product availability).
